content:
Alex: heads-up — we just got a customer SLA escalation: p99 spiked from 220ms -> ~1.2s after last runtime rollout (v2026.04.12).
Ria: thanks, which tenant? any error rates?
Alex: tenant acme-inc. No 5xx, just latency regressions on generate endpoints. p95 also up but not as bad.
support-bot: alert: tenant=acme-inc p99_latency=1187ms p95_latency=312ms window=2026-03-17T08:10..08:40
Mike: copy. Do we have canary cohorts still running? I thought rollout was gradual.
Jordan: can confirm cohort A (10% traffic) still on old runtime, cohort B (40%) on new, rest ramping. Canary metric dashboard shows tail jump aligning with B ramp at 08:12.
Tanvi: dumping quick traces from flame: ``service=inference runtime=worker-v2026.04.12 kernel=sched-v3`` — I see longer queue wait times in many hosts.
Ria: can you paste the query you used for traces?
Tanvi: sure — ``select count(), p95(latency), p99(latency) by host from traces where tenant="acme-inc" and service="generate" since 30m``
Alex: also saw KV cache miss rate increase ~8% for that cohort at same time. possible cache invalidation bug?
Mike: if KV misses + queueing, could be a scheduling change that favors throughput but increases single-request latency. Did the rollout include the new scheduler?
Jordan: yes — the change set included: scheduler fallback PR #487, quantized kernel bump, and a minor auth refresh optimization.
Ria: we need to bisect. Two likely suspects: scheduler and quantized kernel. Auth refresh seems unrelated (no 401s).
Alex: agree. Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback scheduler change for cohort B, 2) re-route acme-inc to cohort A (old runtime), 3) temporarily increase concurrency on affected workers. Which is least risk?
Tanvi: re-route is fastest — update routing policy to send acme-inc to old runtime variant. I can patch route in <5m.
Mike: while Tanvi does that, I'll start reproduction against canary hosts with synthetic load matching acme's seq len distribution. Need a curl example for exact traffic shape.
Jordan: curl example: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","input":"<long prompt>...","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```
Use concurrency 6, inter-arrival matching acme sample (bursty).
Tanvi: routing change applied. acme-inc now directed to runtime v2026.03.30 (previous). Confirming metrics — p99 dropped to ~240ms within 90s. :thumbsup:
Alex: great — that stabilizes customer. Now we should bisect to identify root cause before full rollout.
Ria: plan: isolate scheduler change by deploying new runtime with quant kernel disabled, and separately deploy quant kernel with old scheduler. Test both with same synthetic workload and compare p99.
Mike: I'll run the two ablation tests in parallel on a small cluster. Collect p95/p99 + KV miss rate + queue depth.
Jordan: logging note — add ``SCHED_ACTION`` logging at debug for the scheduler variant so we can see if requests are being delayed for coalescing.
Tanvi: also instrumented cache key TTLs; earlier rollout changed prefixing + TTLs in one commit — could explain KV miss spike. We should include that in bisect.
Alex: good catch. So three bisect axes: scheduler, quant kernel, cache key change. Use progressive binary search across commits.
Ria: timeline: Mike runs ablation tests (15m each) -> post results here -> if scheduler reproduces, we rollback scheduler across rollout and re-run. If cache change reproduces, hotfix the key prefix.
Mike: starting tests now. kicking off two jobs: job-709999-a (old-sched + new-quant), job-709999-b (new-sched + old-quant).
ops-bot: deploy job-709999-a started on cluster-canary-3
ops-bot: deploy job-709999-b started on cluster-canary-4
Jordan: also enabling trace sampling at 100% for acme-inc for next 10m to catch tail behaviors.
Alex: communicate to support that we've routed them back and are doing deep triage. Ria, can you send a short note to the customer?
Ria: on it. Message: "We've routed your workload to the previous runtime variant to meet your SLA and are actively bisecting the rollout cause. We'll update within 2 hours or sooner."
Tanvi: job-709999-a p99=260ms p95=210ms KV_miss=6% queue_depth=12
Mike: job-709999-b p99=1.1s p95=320ms KV_miss=14% queue_depth=42 — new-scheduler looks bad here.
Jordan: that points to scheduler change interacting with cache behavior. Maybe scheduler is batching/coalescing more aggressively causing head-of-line blocking when KV misses occur.
Alex: next step: capture per-request timelines and identify where the extra 800ms is spent (queue vs compute vs remote kv). If queue wait is high, tweak scheduler’s max_coalesce_ms down as experiment.
Mike: I can run a quick variant with max_coalesce_ms=4ms (current was 12ms) on canary and run same synthetic load.
Tanvi: rolled out small scheduler tweak to canary-4.
ops-bot: deploy tweak-709999-sched started
Mike: tweak results: p99=420ms p95=260ms KV_miss=13% queue_depth=18 — improved but not back to baseline.
Ria: that suggests both scheduler and cache prefixing contribute. We should revert cache prefix change in the next hotfix and keep scheduler tweak.
Alex: agreed. Action items: 
- Tanvi: prepare hotfix to revert cache prefix TTL commit and ship to canary (ETA 40m).
- Mike: continue run with scheduler tweak and collect longer run metrics (1h).
- Jordan: collate traces and write repro notes (include payloads, workload generator script, and exact cluster IDs).
- Ria: update customer at 1h with findings and plan.
Tanvi: starting hotfix branch now.
Jordan: logging the incident in postmortems channel after we close. Also adding a rollout guard item to block prefix-like config changes without explicit cache-sensitivity review.
Alex: thanks team. Keep updates here. If we re-open traffic to new runtime, do it in smaller steps and watch tail.
Ria: customer updated and acknowledged. "Appreciate the quick routing fix — will monitor and report if anything else."
Mike: will post an initial results summary in 45m.
Alex: linking to dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenants/acme-inc/latency?window=1h
Tanvi: hotfix deployed to canary-3. initial p99=230ms.
Jordan: all right — looks like combined fix removes tail. We'll schedule full rollback vs targeted revert depending on verification run.
Alex: end state for now: traffic routed back to old runtime, hotfix reverted cache change in canary, scheduler tweak applied in canary. Follow-up: decision whether to roll forward with scheduler tweak + cache revert or full rollback of new runtime.
Ria: added follow-up ticket infra#7568 and assigned to Tanvi & Mike.
Alex: thanks everyone. Closing SLA escalation; will reopen if metrics worsen. :white_check_mark:
